Welcome to this journey into the heart of our natural world—a place where silence has begun to settle in the spaces once ruled by nature’s most powerful hunters.
Imagine walking through forests, over grasslands, or even along the edge of the ocean, only to realize something’s missing. The shapes and shadows that once inspired awe—wolves, lions, sharks—are fading away, and with them, the balance of life itself starts to unravel.
In Where the Wild Things Were: Life, Death, and Ecological Wreckage in a Land of Vanishing Predators, William Stolzenburg takes us deep into this unfolding story. Together, we’ll explore how the loss of these top predators doesn’t just affect the animals themselves, but transforms entire landscapes—sometimes in ways you’d never expect.
You’ll see what happens when prey run rampant, when forests struggle to survive, and even when rivers change their course. It’s a powerful reminder of just how connected everything is—and how a single missing piece can shake the whole puzzle.
But this isn’t just a story of loss. Along the way, we’ll meet scientists, conservationists, and everyday people who are working to restore what’s been lost—sparking new debates, fresh hope, and innovative solutions that just might turn things around.
So, as we dive into these tangled webs of life, let’s reflect together on our own role in shaping the future—because the story of vanishing predators is, in many ways, a story about us all.
